Category or scenario: AUB: no pelvic ultrasound within 12 months
Our understanding of the rule: If there is no pelvic ultrasound within 12 months, the referral appears to be rejected and returned to GP requesting re-referral with scan.

Category or scenario: AUB: endometrial thickness >15mm or no recent endometrial sample, with or without adenomyosis
Our understanding of the rule: If ultrasound shows endometrial thickness >15mm and there is no pipelle or endometrial sample in the last 6 months, with or without adenomyosis, this appears to be P2 Menorrhagia.
What information does the grader need to: Ultrasound findings, endometrial thickness, biopsy history

Category or scenario: AUB: ultrasound suggestive of polyp
Our understanding of the rule: If ultrasound is suggestive of polyp, with or without dysmenorrhoea, this appears to be P3 Hysteroscopy.

Category or scenario: AUB: ET <15mm, otherwise normal, but bleeding >3 months and medical management already tried
Our understanding of the rule: If ET <15mm and otherwise normal, but intermenstrual or continuous bleeding has lasted >3 months and medical management has been tried, this appears to be P3 Menorrhagia. If not tried, the note appears to suggest medical treatment first.
Expected outcome or priority: P3 Menorrhagia or medical management first

Category or scenario: AUB: post-coital bleeding with normal smear in premenopausal patient
Our understanding of the rule: Post-coital bleeding with normal smear in a premenopausal patient appears not to need specialist review.
Expected outcome or priority: Does not need to be seen

Category or scenario: AUB: fibroid <3cm found incidentally on ultrasound
Our understanding of the rule: If ultrasound shows fibroid <3cm, no other abnormalities, and normal ET, this appears to be declined with advice that the fibroid is incidental. If medical management has already been tried, it appears to become P3 Gynae.
What information does the grader need to: Ultrasound, fibroid size, endometrial thickness, prior management
Expected outcome or priority: Decline or P3 depending on prior management

Category or scenario: AUB: abnormal cervix with normal smear
Our understanding of the rule: If there is an abnormal cervix with normal smear, this appears to be P2 Gynae and requires SMO grading.

Category or scenario: PMB: no ultrasound within 6 months
Our understanding of the rule: If there is no ultrasound within 6 months, the referral appears to be rejected and sent back requesting ultrasound. The note suggests POAC if cost is a barrier.

Category or scenario: PMB: single episode with ET <4mm
Our understanding of the rule: Single episode PMB with ET <4mm appears to suggest community pipelle if appropriate, ovestin cream, and re-referral only if PMB recurs.

Category or scenario: PMB: one or more episodes with ET >=5mm
Our understanding of the rule: One or more episodes of PMB with ET >=5mm appears to be HSC P1 and Rapid Access Clinic hysteroscopy.

Category or scenario: PMB: multiple episodes with ET <5mm
Our understanding of the rule: Multiple episodes of PMB with ET <5mm also appear to be HSC P1 / Rapid Access Clinic.

Category or scenario: PMB: other ultrasound abnormalities
Our understanding of the rule: If ultrasound shows other abnormalities, the note appears to require SMO-only grading and clinical judgement.

Category or scenario: Fibroids >3cm with mass symptoms or hydronephrosis
Our understanding of the rule: Fibroids >3cm with mass symptoms, and/or hydronephrosis, appear to be P2 Gynae.

Category or scenario: Fibroids <3cm with mass symptoms
Our understanding of the rule: Fibroids <3cm with mass symptoms appear to be P3 Gynae, with a note to GP to explore other causes as well.

Category or scenario: Fibroids <3cm with no mass symptoms or AUB
Our understanding of the rule: Fibroids <3cm with no mass symptoms or AUB appear to be declined and do not need follow-up scan.

Category or scenario: Ovarian masses or cysts: probable benign cyst
Our understanding of the rule: Probable benign ovarian cysts, including simple cyst or likely dermoid, appear to be Gynae P2.

Category or scenario: Ovarian masses or cysts: suspicious complex adnexal mass
Our understanding of the rule: Complex adnexal masses that appear suspicious seem to require SMO-only grading, CT if age >40, tumour markers for all ages, and HSC P1 if clinically appropriate.
What information does the grader need to: Mass features, imaging, tumour markers, age

Category or scenario: HSC P2 semi-urgent category
Our understanding of the rule: HSC P2 appears to be an SMO-only category for concerning referrals that do not meet HSC P1 but should not wait the standard P2 timeframe. The guideline examples include borderline ovarian cyst, recurrent PMB with normal histology, and premenopausal referral with markedly increased ET.

Category or scenario: Pelvic pain: no ultrasound
Our understanding of the rule: No ultrasound appears to lead to rejection unless there is already a strong endometriosis history or other exception.

Category or scenario: Pelvic pain: >3 months with normal ultrasound
Our understanding of the rule: Pelvic pain >3 months with normal ultrasound appears to be P3.

Category or scenario: Pelvic pain: endometrioma >=5cm or DIE on imaging
Our understanding of the rule: Abnormal ultrasound with endometrioma >=5cm or DIE on imaging appears to be P2.

Category or scenario: Pelvic pain: chronic pelvic pain fully investigated and gynae cause treated
Our understanding of the rule: If chronic pelvic pain has been fully investigated and the gynaecological cause has been treated, the note appears to decline and refer to Chronic Pain Service.
Expected outcome or priority: Decline / refer to Chronic Pain Service

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: mesh problems
Our understanding of the rule: Mesh-related problems appear to be P2 and SMO-reviewed.

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: procidentia
Our understanding of the rule: Procidentia appears to be P2.

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: prolapse without procidentia
Our understanding of the rule: Prolapse without procidentia appears to be P3.

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: prolapse with urinary retention
Our understanding of the rule: Prolapse with urinary retention appears to be P2.

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: stress incontinence
Our understanding of the rule: Stress urinary incontinence appears to be P3.

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: urge incontinence without prior medication trial
Our understanding of the rule: Urge incontinence appears to be rejected unless medications have already been tried.

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: asymptomatic prolapse
Our understanding of the rule: Asymptomatic prolapse appears to be rejected.

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology: previous TVT or sling issue
Our understanding of the rule: Previous TVT or sling issue appears to be P2 and SMO-reviewed.

Category or scenario: Fertility
Our understanding of the rule: Fertility referrals appear to be declined and redirected to Northern Region Fertility Service.

Category or scenario: PCOS
Our understanding of the rule: PCOS appears to be managed virtually and not seen face-to-face unless diagnosis is unclear or fertility issues require SMO input.

Category or scenario: Cervical polyp: asymptomatic and <=2cm with normal smear
Our understanding of the rule: Asymptomatic cervical polyp <=2cm with normal smear appears to be rejected with GP monitoring.

Category or scenario: Cervical polyp: >=2cm with normal smear and symptoms
Our understanding of the rule: Cervical polyp >=2cm with normal smear and symptoms such as post-coital or intermenstrual bleeding appears to be P3 Gynaecology.

Category or scenario: Paediatric gynaecology and structural anomalies
Our understanding of the rule: These referrals appear to need SMO grading and may need transfer to paediatric or female multi-disciplinary services depending on the scenario.
What information does the grader need to: Age, presenting issue, imaging, tumour markers

Category or scenario: Pelvic tear
Our understanding of the rule: 3A tear appears to be referred to Women's Health physio. 3B, 3C, and 4th degree tears appear to be P3.
Expected outcome or priority: Physio or P3 depending on grade

Category or scenario: Tubal ligation counselling
Our understanding of the rule: Tubal ligation counselling (MSC) appears to be P3.

Category or scenario: Re-grading patients already on the waitlist
Our understanding of the rule: Patients already on the waitlist who are re-referred with updated information appear to require re-grading and booking-team notification if the priority changes.
Expected outcome or priority: Re-grade and update waitlist if needed
